questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. I found a place on AirBnB with two friends.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: To find an affordable place off campus may be a bit far away from the city centrum. Therefore you must prepare yourself on taking the bus a lot.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They had timeslots and you could just sign in whenever it made sense. The employees of the university was very helpful and it was quickly done.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Information online.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Quite successful. I didn't get the courses I wanted but ended up with some interesting stuff after all.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be adherent to the fact that the course program of the semester that you're going to do won't be made available to see until right before the semester starts.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I actually found the teaching a bit underwhelming. The lectures were to short and so was the class interactions. There were hardly any time to get into the stuff that we were discussion. I also thought that the level were a bit to low and not so demanding.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A bit underwhelming.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *

questions.answer: Hmm don't know...

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots of sport clubs and student societies. Lots of things to do every week if interested.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I went a lot to the film society of the university. They showed a lot of great movies throughout the semester and it was very cheap! Can really recommend!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the highlands! It's actually affordable. And also go and see the other cities that are located around Edinburgh - Glasgow etc. I would also recommend the many museums of the city. They are free and very nice. Also a lot of great and cheap food options.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very pleasing and nice. The locals very so talkative and very friendly. I never felt unsafe.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just take it easy. They are very accommodating and talkative. It's not that hard to start a conversation. Otherwise you can always go for a pint/soda at a bar.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It could be a bit hard to understand some of the locals because of the Scottish dialect. Also, it took some time to transfer the economic system of my home country to pounds.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Food, drinks, nature, the people and the beautiful architecture of the city.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't stress about housing or accommodation. The staff and university are very helpful and you will eventually find a place. 

Money! The city is expensive. Be prepared and hopefully have some money with you from the start. There are cheaper options though, but overall quite expensive. 

Find time to explore the city and the country of Scotland. I didn't find the semester that stressfull, so take the weekends off to do something fun, both in Edinburgh but also in Glasgow, Dundee, Highlands and other wonderful places of Scotland!!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Always just go physically to the exchange student office to get help. Much easier than writing mails and they are very friendly and helpsome.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning about Scotland and the Scottish people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finance, in some way. Otherwise not very challenging. I found the university and the people I met overall very helpful and friendly. I never found myself alone or so confused that I couldn't find the best solution to my problems.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
